title: Finding Registry Entry
description: One JSON object per line in findings.jsonl. Hash-chained append-only state store for every CATCHER-produced finding in the enterprise-v2 review cycle. Consumed by tools/gates/finding-registry.ts CLI (Phase 2), commit-msg-validator.ts (Phase 2), finding-state-sweep.yml (Phase 6 cron), and root-cause-auditor (Phase 5).

oneOf.$comment: Named carve-out grandfathering FARM-DATAMIG-001 (commit 6b372511, appended 2026-04-24) per docs/reviews/orphan-findings.md#ORPHAN-012. The CLASSIFIER alternation in the sibling pattern branch requires CLASSIFIER ∈ {CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, CVE} but this single historical entry uses the domain tag `DATAMIG` as its CLASSIFIER. Because findings.jsonl is a hash-chained append-only ledger, rewriting the entry would invalidate every subsequent prev_hash pointer (the exact corruption pattern the integrity invariant exists to detect — see tests/invariants/finding-registry-integrity.spec.ts hash-chain checks). The const branch ONLY admits this exact literal id; different malformed ids (e.g. FARM-FOOBAR-001) still fail because they match neither branch. Do NOT add DATAMIG to the sibling pattern alternation — that would conflate severity-classifier with domain-tag and invite further drift. If a second one-off grandfather case ever arises, append another const branch here, not a regex relax.

id.description: Finding ID per _shared/output-format.md. Format: {PREFIX}-{CLASSIFIER}-{NNN}. CLASSIFIER is usually severity (CRITICAL|HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW); CVE is a separate classifier for findings sourced from CVE databases (RUSTSEC/GHSA etc.) whose identity is upstream-stable even as severity mutates. P0 reserved for Phase-0 audit bootstrap. PRODUCT-* reserved for test-agents lane-B (Phase 13). DEPLOY-* reserved for deploy-resilience findings (ADR-016 class). RUST-* reserved for Rust sidecar (sens-api-gateway, sensor-ingestion) findings. ULTRA-* reserved for ultra-plan gap-closure batches (sens-api-gateway 2026-04-24 plan). ORPHAN-* reserved for cross-cutting orphan findings registered against docs/reviews/orphan-findings.md anchors. RBAC-* reserved for the tenant/superadmin RBAC end-to-end audit cycle (2026-07-11-rbac-e2e-audit). Other prefixes match agent finding-id-prefix sections. The `oneOf` shape allows a single named-const carve-out for the historical malformed entry FARM-DATAMIG-001 (see ORPHAN-012).

severity.description: Match severity in the id field.

state.description: Lifecycle state. OPEN = raised, no commit. IN-PROGRESS = in an implementation-planner package. RESOLVED = merged commit carries matching Closes: line. STALE = 30 days OPEN without movement. BLOCKED = escalated to architectural-arbiter or awaiting override.

title.description: One-line human-readable summary. Hard cap raised from 200 to 400 chars to accommodate INFRA-* + DEPLOY-* entries whose titles legitimately span multiple causes (e.g. 'Migration X failed because of Y AND Z, blocking deploy round N'). Above 400 chars, decompose into multiple findings.

layer.description: Layer-1 (tech) / Layer-2 (pattern) / Layer-3 (ADR) per the 3-layer knowledge model. Layers 4 and 5 admitted for cross-layer findings used by INFRA-* + RUST-CVE-* entries (4 = ops/infra concern, 5 = supply-chain/CVE). Optional — not every finding fits the layer taxonomy.

evidence.description: Evidence citation — non-empty string with no leading/trailing whitespace. Canonical shapes documented for CATCHER agents: 'file:line' (code reference), 'file:start-end' (line range), 'file:test_name' (test function ref), 'file (test_name)' (parenthesized test ref, used by sens-api-gateway Rust suite), 'file#anchor' (markdown plan / ADR anchor), or just 'file' (whole-file evidence). The schema previously enforced the path-shape regex `^[^\s:]+(:[^\s:]+(-[^\s:]+)?)?(\s*\(.*\))?(#[A-Za-z0-9._-]+)?$`; that constraint was relaxed (architectural-arbiter rationale, plan §2 Option A in /tmp/ci-cleanup-plans/invariants-deferred.md) because (a) it rejected legitimate evidence shapes that emerged in real CATCHER output — Rust `path::method` item-paths, droplet diagnostic prose with embedded colons, CI run/log references, and tail-after-paren context — and (b) the registry is hash-chained append-only so historical entries cannot be rewritten to fit a tighter schema. Discipline at the path-shape level is enforced upstream by tests/invariants/finding-evidence-shape.spec.ts (advisory Tier-3, future-only gate on created_at >= 2026-05-10). At least one entry required for CRITICAL/HIGH per the allOf rule below.

rule_violated.description: Named rule: ADR number + title, ESLint rule ID, CLAUDE.md section, or layer-1/2/3 entry.

owner_agent.description: Agent that raised the finding. Must be a name in orchestrator.md runtime roster.

raised_in_cycle.description: Review cycle identifier — YYYY-MM-DD-{topic} matching docs/reviews/{agent}/{file}.md naming.

review_file.description: Path to the review markdown file that first documented this finding. Relative to repo root.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of first state transition to OPEN.

closed_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of transition to RESOLVED. null while not RESOLVED.

closing_commits.description: Git SHAs of commits whose message contains 'Closes: ...#<this-id>'. Populated by closes-footer-check workflow.

deadline.description: Deadline for BLOCKED state (override protocol) or for tracked planner packages. null otherwise. Accepts either ISO 8601 calendar-date (`YYYY-MM-DD`, the canonical writer convention used by ULTRA-* / RUST-CVE-* / INFRA-CRITICAL-*) OR full RFC 3339 date-time (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`, used by ORPHAN-HIGH-035/039 and ULTRA-HIGH-071 which carry explicit end-of-day timestamps to remove ambiguity about when the day expires). Both shapes convey the same semantic — `date-time` is strictly more precise than `date` — so admitting either is the architectural fix rather than rewriting the three outlier entries (which would corrupt the hash chain). Future writers should default to the calendar-date shape unless they have a reason to encode a specific time-of-day.

owner_user.description: GitHub handle accountable for closing. Required when state is BLOCKED.

override_of.description: If this entry represents an auditor-override (a Tier-4 exception tracked via inline comment), this field points to the underlying finding ID being overridden. null otherwise.

prev_hash.description: SHA-256 of the previous entry's content_hash (64 zeros for the first entry). Enables tamper-evident append-only chain.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 of this entry's JSON serialization with prev_hash and content_hash fields excluded. Computed and stamped at write time by tools/gates/finding-registry.ts CLI.

notes.description: Free-text notes. No structural requirements; avoid sensitive data — the jsonl is committed to the repo.

narrative.description: Free-form multi-paragraph context entries, captured when an incident note is too large for a single `notes` string and is not a precise `file:line` citation that belongs in `evidence`. Optional companion to `evidence`; `evidence` remains the canonical locus for file:line references.
